task: Projectwise v3.7.0 — readable .md rule mirror (~/.claude/rules-md) with .toon round-trip; rules/ becomes strictly .toon-only; cpm rules-sync bootstrap
decisions: Mirror at ~/.claude/rules-md/ holding readable .md masters + a <stem>.toon symlink to the live rules .toon.
rules/ made strictly .toon-only (the 4 live .md were compiled and removed); user accepted that Claude Code natively loads .md and .toon-only needs their own loader.

Reused the user's existing converter pipeline `md_to_json | toon -e -o` (same as their rules-to-toon.sh hook) instead of reimplementing; Projectwise runs it itself because $EDITOR edits don't trigger that hook.
Safety: .toon written atomically via temp; on converter failure master kept + old .toon preserved; .md removed from rules/ only after non-empty .toon written.
Edit flow now operates on the persistent master in rules-md (no temp file), recompiling on save.
outcome: Implemented, tested, installed. cargo build --release clean; clippy 0 errors (2 pre-existing); 12/12 tests. rules-sync built 21 masters + 21 symlinks; rules/ now .toon-only; round-trip + idempotency verified. FINDING: 4 rules (aqua-agent, docker-permissions, document-auto-processing, mcp-architecture) were already gone before rules-sync (user's ~21:00 _backups_mcp_cleanup); rules-sync never deletes .toon. aqua-agent recoverable from backups; other 3 have no local backup. Not committed/pushed.
